industry.src: AR FY26 management discussion (industry estimates quoted by the company); Q1FY27 call (biryani market)
notes: Delivery has moved from under 10% of KFC's sales before Covid to ~45% (Q1FY27 call): aggregators now take share from dine-in rather than adding to it, and their own cheap-meal formats compete on price.

Three Yum! franchisees in India before the merger: Devyani (north, east, central), Sapphire Foods (south, west, Sri Lanka) and Yum! itself (19 KFC stores in Hyderabad, which Devyani will buy). Pizza Hut has been run through a three-way structure (Devyani, Sapphire, Yum!) that management blames for slow decisions.
KFC SSSG was negative for about 13 quarters to Q3FY26; it turned positive in Q4FY26 (+4.9%) and Q1FY27 (+3.3%).

excluded.RBA: Restaurant Brands Asia's consolidated EBITDA was negative or near zero (Indonesia losses) from Oct-2021 to May-2022, so Screener has no EV/EBITDA for 35 of the 261 weeks: no complete five-year median (same treatment as JUBLFOOD.ctx.js). Shown as a sensitivity row.

peers.note: QSR set fixed by the Jubilant FoodWorks report (JUBLFOOD.ctx.js), with Devyani itself replaced by Jubilant. The metric is EV/EBITDA (Screener, trailing, leases in EV); QSR P/Es are meaningless (Westlife, Sapphire and Devyani earn almost nothing after depreciation of right-of-use assets). Sapphire listed 18-Nov-2021 and misses 7 weeks of the window (Metro Brands precedent). Sapphire is the merger partner: since 1-Jan-2026 its price has moved with Devyani's through the 177:100 swap ratio, so an ex-Sapphire row is shown; the base keeps the house set. Three usable names, so the retail set (DMART.ctx.js) and a widened QSR + retail set are sensitivity rows.

points: Promoter-controlled (RJ Corp 57.98%); the group also controls Varun Beverages. Related-party dealings are small (FY26: purchases from Varun Beverages Rs19.6 cr, rent to Global Health Rs6.4 cr); the Arctic International purchase of 18.5% of Sapphire (an RJ Corp company) was dropped in Aug-2026.
Thailand is held 51:49 with Camas (Temasek); Camas has a put option on the RJ Corp holding company, not on Devyani; Devyani has a call option it has not booked (AR FY26).
FY26: CEO change (Virag Joshi to Manish Dawar from 1-Apr-2026); Mr Dawar exercised 27 lakh options (Rs26.9 cr perquisite) on top of Rs5.8 cr pay while the company lost money.

Joint auditors (Walker Chandiok, O P Bagla); unmodified opinion; key audit matter on impairment of Rs1,722 cr of goodwill, brands, territory and franchise rights. Thai CGU flagged an impairment indicator (performance below the acquisition case) but no impairment was booked.

moat.verdict: Narrow at best. Devyani's advantage is contractual, not owned: exclusive Yum! development rights for KFC and Pizza Hut in its territories, renewable at Yum!'s discretion, for a royalty of ~6.5% of revenue. KFC's brand is strong and chicken is the fastest-growing QSR category, but the brand belongs to Yum!, new chicken chains and aggregator meals are easy to try, and Pizza Hut has lost share to Domino's for years. Scale (2,255 stores) gives procurement and site-selection benefits that the Sapphire merger would roughly double.

critiques.view: The stock is a call on KFC SSSG, and SSSG is only +3%
critiques.detail: After 13 negative quarters, KFC SSSG was +4.9% (Q4FY26) and +3.3% (Q1FY27); management guides 5-6% and admits the macro (LPG, rupee, crude) is not stable. Margins depend on ADS reaching Rs105-110k from Rs98k.

critiques.view: Earnings are near zero and the P/E is meaningless
critiques.detail: Net profit after minorities -Rs38.6 cr in FY26, Rs14.6 cr in Q1FY27. Depreciation of right-of-use assets and lease interest absorb almost all of the EBITDA; the street prices it on pre-Ind AS EV/EBITDA two years out.

critiques.view: Half of Thailand belongs to Temasek
critiques.detail: Camas owns 49% of the Thai holding company (52.45% effective). Valuing consolidated EBITDA at a multiple without deducting them overstates the equity by ~14%.

critiques.view: The merger is the story, but it is not done
critiques.detail: CCI and NCLT approvals were pending on 30-Sep-2026; Devyani issues 56.9 cr shares (46% dilution) for Sapphire, pays ~Rs320 cr to Yum!, and the RJ Corp group falls to 42%. Synergies (Rs210-225 cr) are management's estimate.
Pizza Hut India revenue fell in FY26 (-1.6%) and Q1FY27 (-1.6%), stores cut from 639 to 626, brand contribution negative; management will 'push' it only after the merger (FY28).

gaps: Thailand EBITDA is not disclosed separately; we assume it is 91% of International EBITDA (its revenue share).
India post-Ind AS EBITDA for Q1FY27 is not disclosed (only pre-Ind AS).
Sapphire Foods is not modelled in detail; the pro-forma sensitivity grows its FY26 EBITDA at our Devyani rate.
Citi's reported target (May-2026) could not be verified from a public source dated before 30-Sep-2026 and is left out of the street table.
Anand Rathi's 30-Jul-2026 note was read only through a DSIJ summary; whether its 16x EV/EBITDA is pre- or post-Ind AS is not stated.
No Q2FY27 data used (results due by mid-November 2026).
KFC India store count at Mar-2024 not in our sources, so FY25 revenue per average store is not shown.
conflicts: The presentation's India revenue (FY26 Rs3,793 cr) is Rs41 cr above the AR geographic figure (Rs3,752 cr): the difference is eliminated on consolidation; we use the AR figure so that India + International = consolidated revenue.

Screener's EBITDA (FY26 Rs860 cr, FY24 Rs565 cr) differs from the company's (Rs855 cr, Rs652 cr): Screener reclassifies some items; we use the company basis for the forward multiple and the forecasts.
Two broker notes dated 30-Jul-2026 show a CMP of Rs118 while DSIJ quotes Rs138.55: we use only the targets and methods.
